tfn.s: The survey asked workers in 36 countries.
tfn.why: The text says: "Adecco asked 40,500 workers in 36 countries"

tfn.s: The results mean that money has stopped mattering to workers.
tfn.why: The text says: "The results do not mean that money has stopped mattering"

tfn.s: Most workers in the survey want to work from home every day.
tfn.why: The text does not say how many workers want to work from home every day.

focus.note: Some verbs and adjectives go together naturally. Think about which word you usually hear before or after the other.

tfn.s: The report appeared several months after the workers were questioned.
tfn.why: The questions were asked in June and July, but the report came out on 19 November 2026.

tfn.s: The text says that every worker is free to give up pay for more free time.
tfn.why: A worker struggling with rent, bills and food prices "may not have that option".

tfn.s: The survey found that women want flexibility more than men do.
tfn.why: The text does not say whether women or men want flexibility more.

tfn.s: Giving one department more freedom than another can cause problems.
tfn.why: The text says that if one department gets more freedom, "tensions can build up".

tfn.s: The text says flexible hours give struggling workers more peace of mind than higher wages.
tfn.why: The text says: "higher wages can provide the peace of mind that flexible hours cannot"

focus.note: Collocations are word pairs that sound natural together. Check the noun that comes after the gap and think of the verb or adjective partner.

tfn.s: The findings may not predict how people would act when given a real job offer.
tfn.why: The survey records stated priorities, "not proof" that people would reject higher pay.

tfn.s: The survey covered more countries than industries.
The fieldwork was carried out in the same month that the report appeared.
tfn.why: Fieldwork took place in June and July; the report was released in November.

tfn.s: Workers with the longest commutes were the most likely to name work-life balance as their main reason.
tfn.why: The text does not link commute length to the survey answers.

tfn.s: The writer argues that a high salary always makes a job worthwhile.
tfn.why: The text says a well-paid job "can still be a poor bargain" if it leaves little time or energy.

speak.title: Role-play: a better deal at work
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your employee wants to change their working hours. The shop is busy in the evenings and you need enough staff. Ask at least two questions before you decide. You can say yes, no, or yes with a condition.

b.text: You would like to start earlier and finish earlier so you can be home for your family. You could accept a little less pay. Explain why this matters to you and how the work will still get done.

phrases: I'd like to talk about my working hours.
I'd be happy to earn a bit less if I could finish earlier.
It'd make a big difference to my family.
How would the team cover the busy evenings?
I'm afraid we can't change everyone's hours.
Could we try it for a month and see how it goes?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you agree a deal, and was it fair for the rest of the team?
